algorithm: SPEC.md §7 and §5.2 (APRV-510, proposed): the `exec.code` class for opaque agent code, closed unless the attested policy declares `exec.code.custody: attested` (and, for Hermes `execute_code`, `exec.code.execute_code: hooked`)
description: Per-harness PreToolUse envelopes over a scratch gate whose policy text each vector carries, with any file a program names written into the gate root first (`<gate>` in a string is that root). The expectation pins the permission, the deny CODE, the class of an `execution.started` or an `approval.requested` the call appended, and, where the vector names a `secret` its program carries, that the program text reached neither the log nor the payload store. Three things are pinned from both sides: a policy that never names exec.code refuses every form as it did before the class existed; a policy that names it without custody refuses `hook-exec-code-custody-unattested`; and the shapes outside the class (`bash -c`, a pipe into an interpreter, a shell-expanded program word, a skill script, a program inside a subshell) keep their answers when it is open. A file program is refused `hook-exec-code-unreadable` unless the hook can place it by the kernel's reading: no `..`, a directory that is its own realpath, the line's sole segment, and a working directory the harness states (`symlinks` and `cwd` in a vector's input set those up). The control is a policy with an unknown `exec.code` key, which must fail closed.
provenance: Generated by scripts/regen-conformance-vectors.mjs from this repository's own implementation. Inputs are authored by hand; every expectation is computed, never transcribed. See conformance/README.md for the runner contract.
